extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants seeking NIH funding (R01, K awards, K99, F fellowships, R35 MIRA, SBIR/STTR, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, community-sourced guidance and procedural criteria for preparing, submitting, responding to review, and interpreting status/actions for NIH grant applications across multiple mechanisms. Covers resubmission strategy, study section/SEP issues, JIT/administrative review signals, paylines/select-pay, and award-processing roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission eligibility (A1 → A0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The A1 status doesn’t matter – you can submit again as a new A0 (it’s not like a K99 or other mechanism with finite application window).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check mechanism-specific rules (some mechanisms like K99 may have eligibility windows). After receiving the summary statement, ask your Program Officer (PO) whether to plan an October resubmission and for advice on addressing reviewer concerns. Treat resubmission as insurance if funding timeline is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Program Official (PO) for next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: When you get your summary statement, you should ask your PO if you should plan to submit again in October and, if so, if they have any advice on the resubmission that would help address the concerns discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs cannot predict funding likelihood until budgets are set, but they can advise whether a resubmission is warranted and provide guidance on content changes. Contact the PO for clarification if council dates/statuses change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of study section/council assignment changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in review assignment, study section, or council date is odd but does not necessarily indicate anything about funding outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such changes can be administrative (e.g., IC changes, reassignments). If ICs change or a secondary IC expresses interest, contact the PO(s) for clarification. Reviewers of resubmissions can see prior summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple ICs / dual-IC significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a primary IC supported by secondary ICs (dual ICs) can mean multiple institutes are interested in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary IC interest can be helpful for funding, but assignment to another IC or council is not a guarantee of funding. PO communication will clarify whether other ICs are advocating for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score/percentile context for funding likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact scores and percentiles matter for funding but thresholds depend on institute paylines and fiscal year appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mid-teens percentile often competitive for fellowships; scores in 20s–30s may be near or just above payline depending on institute and FY. Ask your PO about whether to resubmit. Payline and budget uncertainties (e.g., FY change) limit precise predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-fiscal-year funding patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: End of FY funding decisions may use leftover funds (awards in August/September).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may indicate an application is under end-of-year consideration, but lack of immediate change in eRA does not mean it won’t be funded. If no news by early-September, odds of funding drop rapidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized JIT requests as positive signal
rubrics_metrics.description: A personalized Just-In-Time (JIT) request (especially a second JIT) typically indicates the application is being considered for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a JIT is a good sign, it is not a guarantee until a Notice of Award (NOA) is issued. Expect pending administrative review periods to last weeks to months; GMS will contact you if more info is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Pending administrative review' / 'Pending' status
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons status changes such as 'Pending Administrative Review' or 'Pending' can indicate administrative processing related to an award, but may also reflect other administrative actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume an award until NOA. Contact PO for clarification but recognize PO may be outside final award processing; Grants Management Specialist (GMS) handles administrative actions. Status changes can be caused by staffing or processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of PO vs Grants Management Specialist (GMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: POs provide programmatic advice and advocate for applications but are often outside the award processing loop; GMS handles award paperwork and administrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO can advise on whether to resubmit and interpret summary statements; GMS will request or process JIT and NOA. If GMS is slow or unlisted, check with PO and escalate to branch chief if needed (for guidance, not complaint).

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP (Special Emphasis Panel) vs standing Study Section continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on timing and volume, NIH may place continuous submissions into a SEP rather than the standing study section; SEPs can lack continuity and perceived reviewer expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuity matters, apply on standard deadlines to use a known standing panel. You can list required expertise and non-preferred reviewers in the PHS Assignment Request form; contacting the SRO in advance may help pre-allocate reviewers for late submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the PHS Assignment Request to request/avoid reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You can list anyone on the SEP and standing SRG as a reviewer you do not want and provide objective rationale; this goes in the PHS Assignment Request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide objective reasons (e.g., competition) when listing non-preferred reviewers. Do not refer to prior review or argue about process in the application text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous submission timing constraint (A1 summary statement requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application is considered under review until the summary statement is issued, so you cannot submit a new A0 while the previous A1's summary statement has not been released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the SRO to learn the latest date a continuous submission can be accepted for review in a standing SRG and plan resubmissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO pre-allocation of reviewers as an accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Letting the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) know you'll submit a revised proposal late can allow the SRO to pre-allocate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be at SRO discretion but can help preserve standing study section review for late/continuous submissions. Ask the SRO early if you plan a late submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid formal complaints about review anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not formally complain about SEP or review-process anomalies because that can block future productive interactions; instead use available procedural avenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PHS assignment requests and PO/SRO discussions to address concerns, and save discussions of process from appearing in future applications (they are not relevant to science).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-limit violations and potential withdrawal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative notes that 'page limit for one section of the application may have been exceeded by including excess text in one or more application sections' are serious; NIH can withdraw noncompliant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council may view excess text as an unfair advantage; IC Director can decide to withdraw an application anytime up until NOA. Ensure strict compliance with page limits; if you receive such a note, discuss implications with PO but recognize withdrawal is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select pay / R56 and other bridge options
rubrics_metrics.description: Some applications near but below the payline can be considered for R56 or select-pay bridge awards, often later in the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R56 consideration is not automatic — your PO must advocate for it. R56 awards can be made until Sept 30 for that FY. Ask PO whether you are on the list and whether to resubmit if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting eRA timelines and retrospective award possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH can sometimes fund applications from a prior FY in a later FY (e.g., FY2020 app funded in FY2021), and status changes can reflect administrative moves unrelated to funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may not always be informed immediately of OD or IC-level decisions. Don’t assume; wait for official GMS/NOA communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic choice between mechanisms (MIRA R35 vs R01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive choices (e.g., NIGMS R35 MIRA vs R01) have programmatic tradeoffs: MIRA can provide programmatic support but may restrict future targeted funding from that IC; NIGMS may favor R35s to 'spread the wealth'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is generally unlikely you can 'choose' one if both appear fundable. Consider start dates (MIRA may start earlier), amount of funding, renewal likelihood, career goals, and talk with your PO before declining an award. Supplements (diversity, re-entry) may help cover personnel gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing implications for start-up funds and award start dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Award start dates vary by mechanism and FY; accepting an earlier-starting award can preserve start-up funds and reduce financial pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award (e.g., MIRA) would start in September while an alternative award (e.g., R01) might not start until spring due to budget timing, take account of institutional start-up needs and downstream funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplements to cover salaries or specific needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplements (diversity, re-entry) can sometimes be used to support personnel salaries, though some mechanisms (e.g., competitive revision for ESI MIRA) may not permit competitive revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore supplement options with your PO and IC policies to cover personnel if primary award funding is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about reviewer access to prior summary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers of resubmissions will be able to see prior summary statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume continuity of knowledge; when evaluating whether to change study section, compare rosters to see if prior reviewers migrated to a new panel and note that SROs may assign prior reviewers to maintain continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: If GMS disappears or delays, escalate carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: GMS staffing changes or removal from eRA listing can cause processing delays; this may be common near end-of-year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO is unresponsive by a reasonable date (e.g., mid-August for end-of-FY decisions), consider contacting PO's supervisor (branch chief/division head) for guidance on whether to prepare for fall submissions — do so to get guidance, not to complain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting small changes in council dates/status
rubrics_metrics.description: Council meeting date changes or reassignment to other councils/panels could reflect administrative reassignments and are not definitive evidence of funding or non-funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask PO for clarification; watch for JIT requests or status changes that more strongly indicate consideration for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical timeline expectation for pending decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The pending period between JIT/pending administrative review and NOA can range from a few weeks to several months, commonly around 4–5 weeks but sometimes longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be patient; GMS are busy at fiscal year end. Avoid contacting GMS unless requested; check status with PO for higher-level confirmation that you remain in the queue.

rubrics_metrics.name: General advice about applying on time vs late continuous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying on the standard deadline gives better chance of review in known standing panels and reviewer continuity; continuous submissions risk SEP assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, apply on standard deadlines; if you must submit late, coordinate early with SRO to minimize SEP risk and ask about latest acceptable date for standing SRG review.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI funding-reduction policy ambiguity and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutes have ESI (early-stage investigator) funding reduction policies (e.g., percentage reductions); implementation can vary and there may be disputes about whether ESI status at submission or at award governs the reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If award reductions appear inconsistent with institute guidance, discuss with PO for clarification. Recognize that PO may give mixed signals and institutional communications may be delayed; escalation or formal inquiry may be needed if unresolved.
